note: Re-judged 2026-10-18 (independent auditor, after d12a30ef66). RFC 3579 Section 3: "The NAS-Port or NAS-Port-Id attributes SHOULD be included by the NAS in Access-Request packets"; every EAP-bearing Access-Request ze sends is an admin login's, built by (*radiusAuthenticator).exchange, which now appends NAS-Port-Id from AuthRequest.Service, and the only RADIUS-reaching logins name a channel (ssh/passwordauth.go "ssh", web/auth.go "web"; the API authenticates locally). The L2TP subscriber Access-Request is outside this RFC's scope because it never carries EAP-Message, and it sends NAS-Port anyway. The recorded discrimination breaks (exchange body replaced by panic) only fail the whole login, so they prove nothing about the attribute; auditor overlay mutants did: dropping the NAS-Port-Id append, or passing "" from Authenticate or authenticateEAP, turns the ssh/web EAP subtests and the PAP test red, and a constant "ssh" port turns the web and no-channel subtests red. The tagged negative (no channel, no attribute) checks RFC 2865 Section 5 more than this SHOULD, and its zero-length clause is discharged by EncodeTo, which drops empty attributes (an unconditional-append mutant survives as wire-equivalent); its real value is catching a fixed port. aaa-radius-admin.ci shows the mock server reading nas-port-id=ssh end to end, and web/auth_test.go TestWebLoginsNameTheWebChannel covers the web hand-off untagged.
